docs.title: Resetting Your Password
docs.content: If you've forgotten your password, click 'Forgot password?' on the login screen and enter the email address associated with your account. We'll send you a reset link right away. Click the link and choose a new password that's at least 8 characters long, with at least one number and one uppercase letter. Your new password cannot match any of your previous three passwords. Once you've set a new password, you'll be logged out of all other active sessions for security, and you'll need to sign in again on each device you use. If you don't see the email within a few minutes, check your spam folder, and confirm you're using the same email your admin originally invited you with. Reset emails come from no-reply@solstice.example, so add that address to your safe senders list if your mail provider filters it. Note: password reset links expire after 15 minutes. If yours has expired, don't try to reuse the old email -- just go back to the login page and request a brand new reset link. Each reset link can be used only once. If you did not request a reset, ignore the email; your password will not change unless you open the link. If you keep having trouble, contact your Solstice admin, who can send a new invitation or reset your access.

docs.title: Inviting Team Members
docs.content: Admins can invite new team members from Settings > Team > Invite Member. Enter their email address and choose a role (Viewer, Editor, or Admin). You can invite several people at once by entering multiple email addresses separated by commas, and all of them will receive the same role. They'll receive an email invitation with a link to set up their account. Invitations are valid for 7 days. If an invitation expires or the person never received it, open the Pending tab under Settings > Team, select the invitation, and click Resend. Pending invitations can be cancelled at any time from the same screen. Team members can also be given access to only specific projects, which is useful for contractors or external reviewers. Once a member has joined, you can change their role at any time, as described in Changing User Roles.

docs.title: Exporting Reports to CSV
docs.content: Any report can be exported to CSV from the report toolbar by clicking the download icon and selecting 'Export as CSV'. The export includes all currently visible columns and respects any filters you've applied to the report. Hidden columns are not included, so unhide any column you need before exporting. Dates are exported in ISO 8601 format and numbers are exported without currency symbols, which makes the file easy to open in spreadsheet tools or load into a database. Large exports may take a minute or two to generate, and you'll get a notification when the file is ready to download. Exports are retained for 7 days before being automatically deleted from your download history, so be sure to save a local copy if you'll need it later. Important limit: CSV exports are capped at 10,000 rows. If your report has more rows than that, apply additional filters to narrow it down, or contact support about a bulk data export instead. Exports are logged in the audit log.

docs.title: Understanding Billing Cycles
docs.content: Your billing cycle starts on the day you first subscribed and renews monthly on that same date. If you subscribed on the 31st, renewals on months with fewer days fall on the last day of that month. Invoices are emailed to your billing contact 3 days before each renewal, and you can download past invoices from Settings > Billing > Invoice History. You can update your billing contact or payment method anytime from Settings > Billing. Changes take effect on the next renewal date. If a renewal charge fails, we'll retry twice over the following week before pausing your account. While an account is paused, reports and dashboards are read-only. Refunds for annual plans canceled within the first 30 days are available on request. Tax is calculated based on the billing address on your account, and VAT numbers can be added under Settings > Billing > Tax Details.

docs.title: Setting Up Single Sign-On (SSO)
docs.content: Enterprise plans support SSO via SAML 2.0. To set it up, go to Settings > Security > SSO and provide your identity provider's metadata URL. Common providers include Okta, Azure Active Directory, and Google Workspace, and step-by-step guides for each are available in the developer portal. Once configured, all team members will be redirected to your identity provider to log in. Test the connection with a non-admin account before enforcing SSO for everyone. You can enforce SSO for all users, which disables password login for the organization, or allow password login as a fallback for admins. Certificates used to sign SAML responses expire periodically; you'll get an email reminder 30 days before expiry, and the new certificate can be uploaded from the same SSO page without interrupting logins.

docs.title: API Rate Limits
docs.content: The Solstice API is available on Growth and Enterprise plans. All endpoints are authenticated with an API key passed in the Authorization header, and keys are created under Settings > Developers > API Keys. Responses are returned as JSON, and pagination is handled via a `next_cursor` field in the response body. Pass the cursor back as a query parameter to fetch the next page, and stop when next_cursor is null. We recommend caching responses where possible to avoid unnecessary repeat calls, especially for endpoints that return large datasets. Rate limits: Growth plans are limited to 60 requests per minute, and Enterprise plans are limited to 300 requests per minute, per API key. Exceeding the limit returns an HTTP 429 response, and the Retry-After header tells you how many seconds to wait before retrying. Rotate API keys regularly, and revoke any key that may have been exposed.

docs.title: Two-Factor Authentication
docs.content: Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds a second step to login using an authenticator app. To turn it on, go to Settings > Security > Two-Factor Auth and scan the QR code with an app such as Google Authenticator or Authy. Enter the six-digit code to confirm. Each user enables 2FA for their own account. Admins can require 2FA for every team member from Settings > Security, and members who have not yet enabled it will be prompted at their next login. Backup codes are shown once when 2FA is enabled, so store them somewhere safe; each code can be used only once. If you lose access to your authenticator app, use a backup code to log in, then reset 2FA from your profile. If you have no backup codes and no device, contact your Solstice admin, who can reset 2FA for your account. Codes refresh every 30 seconds, so if a code is rejected, wait for the next one and try again, and make sure your phone's clock is set to automatic time.

docs.title: Scheduling Report Emails
docs.content: Reports can be emailed automatically on a schedule. Open the report, select Schedule, and choose a frequency: daily, weekly, or monthly. For weekly schedules, choose the day of the week, and for monthly schedules, choose a day of the month between 1 and 28. Add one or more recipient email addresses and pick a time zone so the send time matches your local working hours. Scheduled emails attach the report as a CSV file, subject to the same 10,000 row limit as manual exports, and a notice is added to the email body when the report was truncated. To pause a schedule without deleting it, toggle it off on the Schedules page. Recipients outside your organization must be approved by an admin before they receive scheduled reports. Each schedule is logged in the audit log, and admins can see every active schedule from Settings > Security > Schedules.

docs.title: Viewing the Audit Log
docs.content: The audit log records sign-ins, failed sign-in attempts, invitations, role changes, SSO changes, report exports, and scheduled report changes for your organization. Admins can view it from Settings > Security > Audit Log. Entries can be filtered by user, event type, and date range, and each entry shows the time, the acting user, the IP address, and the affected resource. Audit log entries are kept for 12 months. Entries older than 12 months are removed automatically and cannot be recovered. To send the log to an external system such as a SIEM tool, use the audit log export option, which produces a JSON file that can be downloaded or delivered to a configured storage bucket. Only Enterprise plans include the audit log export, and only organization admins can view or export the log.

docs.title: Changing User Roles
docs.content: Admins can change a team member's role at any time from Settings > Team. Click the member's name, select a new role (Viewer, Editor, or Admin), and save. Viewers can only read reports and dashboards and cannot export data. Editors can create and edit reports and dashboards, and can export them, but cannot manage team members. Admins can manage team members, billing contacts, SSO, and security settings. Role changes take effect the next time the user loads a page, and the change is recorded in the audit log. The last remaining Admin in an organization cannot be demoted, so promote another member to Admin before changing your own role.
